events.title: 1Password suffers data breach via compromised GitHub account
events.one_liner: 1Password suffered a data breach on November 19 when an attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account, accessed source code, injected malicious code into backend services, and obtained infrastructure secrets. Customer vaults, passwords, and Secret Keys were not accessed. 1Password rotated credentials and tightened system controls.
takeaways: Breach occurred November 19 via compromised employee GitHub account
Attacker accessed source code, injected malicious code into backend, accessed CI/CD secrets
Exposed data: names, emails, account/user IDs, creation/sign-in dates, public keys, SRP parameters
Customer vault contents, account passwords, Secret Keys not compromised
Invitation/recovery code length increased from 6 to 10 alphanumeric characters
Breach discovered November 19, disclosed November 26
Attacker accessed customer names, emails, account creation/sign-in dates, public keys
Vault data, passwords, encryption keys, recovery keys, Secret Keys not compromised
Revoked stolen token, disabled GitHub account, deployed new detection tools
Users advised to watch for phishing via compromised email addresses

events.title: Prescribed fire reduces giant sequoia mortality by more than half during severe wildfires, study shows
events.one_liner: A study from Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest in California's Sierra Nevada found that prescribed burns cut giant sequoia tree mortality by more than half during the 2020 Castle Fire. The research demonstrates that restoring fire to ecosystems where it was suppressed for nearly 200 years can help these ancient trees survive increasingly severe wildfires.
takeaways: Prescribed fire reduced giant sequoia mortality by more than 50% during the 2020 Castle Fire
Study conducted at Mountain Home Demonstration State Forest, home to the world's largest giant sequoia grove
Findings based on nearly 200 years of fire suppression followed by ecosystem restoration
Research from University of Nevada, Reno College of Agriculture, Biotechnology & Natural Resources
Published August 3, 2026

events.title: California Approves $59.6 Million in Grants for Wildlife Habitat Restoration and Public Access
events.one_liner: Governor Gavin Newsom announced that the Wildlife Conservation Board approved nearly $60 million in grants for 27 biodiversity and habitat restoration projects across 18 California counties. The funding supports wildlife corridors, the California Salmon Strategy, and public access to nature, advancing the state's 30×30 conservation goal.
takeaways: $59.6 million approved for 27 projects across 18 California counties
Includes $5.5 million for wildlife crossings over State Route 62 near Yucca Valley and $4 million for Interstate 15 crossing at Rainbow Canyon to restore habitat connectivity
$2.9 million granted to California Trout Inc. for East Fork Scott River restoration to improve habitat for coho salmon
Projects advance California's 30×30 goal to conserve 30% of state lands and coastal waters by 2030
